title: Baal
author: Robert McCammon
review:
Really enjoyed it. Clearly a product of its time and the race and sexism clearly didn't age well but overall thought it was really well paced and had a lot of variety and had some great writing.

I know McCammon himself is a bit embarrassed about his early work but he doesn't have any reason to be, it contains a lot of the elements that make him a great author, just not fully refined yet. Plenty to dig into and enjoy here and some great ideas and characters.

highlights.text: People died here because they got in the way. Their way of life nursed violence until it was as prevalent and bitter as the hot overhead sun.
“This place is haunted. I hear the mad gods shrieking for revenge. Listen.”

the entire sky was a maelstrom of searing red and whirling black smoke, a chaotic kaleidoscope. The roar of the fires was deafening. It was as if some giant with torch in hand had walked the streets setting everything in sight ablaze.

There are those who say that Baal was born with the mark of heaven. From birth, they say, he was destined to lead men to the gates of greatness. It is only for the future to decide. This is without a doubt the beginning of a new age.…”

Three of the goblets had overturned and the liquid had collected in slimy puddles. Blue clouds of smoke still wafted about the room, swirling like spirits of the dead. Above the odors of smoke and decay there was something else, something that made Virga grind his teeth against its presence. It was the sickly sweet smell of the burial vault.

Where is God? he asked himself. Has man lost himself so hopelessly now that God allows this moment without a single merciful breath? Has Baal grown so strong that even He is struck with terror? The thought chilled him.
“Satan has never been a secondary power; he is the equalizing darkness to Jehovah’s light. At the beginnings the cosmos was created by both Jehovah and Satan.

Their wars will come, yes. Their famines, their droughts. Their crops will turn to dust and their flesh will dry beneath a burning sun, but it will not be by your hand. You’ve begun the decay. I will not allow your power to warp them beyond all redemption.”

“My master and I offer them hate. They take it gladly. They murder and loot and spit on everything you hold sacred. They take our hand and not yours. They praise our name and not yours. They are ours and not yours.”
